# bugs #3992: Duplicate symbol error for an object of an enumerated type that two successive blocks declare

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3992/
- Category: [Trivial fixes](../../fix-trivial.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close. Bug #3495 stays open, because enumeration constants keep the exemption.
- Patch: [bugs-3992.patch](../../patches/bugs-3992.patch), commit [`a5f3514be`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/a5f3514be1ff147dd5c6364b4e7451099931b369). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.

```diff
diff --git a/src/SDCCsymt.c b/src/SDCCsymt.c
index 031677c86..d4337dfae 100644
--- a/src/SDCCsymt.c
+++ b/src/SDCCsymt.c
@@ -2728,7 +2728,12 @@ leaveBlockScope (int block)
               /* Temporary fix for bug #3289 - leave enums in scope. */
               /* This is also buggy but compatible with 4.1.0 and    */
               /* earlier behavior and less likely to trigger errors. */
-              if (sym->etype && SPEC_ENUM(sym->etype))
+              /* It applies to enumeration constants only. BLOCK     */
+              /* nodes do not list them, so resolveSymbols() cannot  */
+              /* mark them as in scope again. Objects and typedef    */
+              /* names of an enumerated type are marked out of scope */
+              /* like the symbols of other types.                    */
+              if (sym->etype && SPEC_ENUM(sym->etype) && IS_LITERAL(sym->etype))
                 continue;
               /* Everything else, mark as out of scope. */
               sym->isinscope = 0;
```
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The function of the ticket has two `for` loops that each declare `Foo_t i`, and the declaration
`int x = 0;` between them. On r17192 the second loop gets error 0, Duplicate symbol 'i', and
error 20, Undefined identifier 'i'. This was reproduced for mcs51 with the small and the large
model. The front end reports the errors, so they do not depend on the port.

## Cause

`leaveBlockScope` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` clears `isinscope` for the symbols of a block when the
parser reaches the end of the block. Since [r13002](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13002/),
the fix for bug #3289, it skips every symbol whose type has the enum flag. Enumeration constants
have that flag, and objects and typedef names of an enumerated type have it too. The `i` of the
first loop therefore stays in scope until the end of the function.

`findSymWithLevel` returns a local symbol of another level only when its `isinscope` is set.
`addSymChain` reports a duplicate when the level of the symbol that `findSymWithLevel` returns
equals the level of the new symbol apart from the sublevel. A declaration that follows a statement
adds a sublevel, so the two declarations of `i` have such levels.

## Fix

`leaveBlockScope` skips a symbol only when its type has the enum flag and the storage class of a
literal, which is true for enumeration constants alone. They keep the exemption for the reason
that a maintainer gives in bug #3289. `BLOCK` nodes do not list enumeration constants, so
`resolveSymbols` cannot set `isinscope` for them again.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3992.c` has the function of the ticket, and a function whose blocks
declare `i` as `int`, `enum tag`, and `long`. On r17192 it does not compile for mcs51-small and
mcs51-large. With the patch it passes on host, the six mcs51 variants (the four models, and small
and large with `--stack-auto`), stm8, and ucz80. For mcs51-small, the code size and the tick count
of every other regression test are unchanged. With the series of this report up to this patch
applied to r17192, the regression suite, which has `bug-3289.c`, has 0 failures for host, the six
mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large,
mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

- Bug #3495 reports error 0 for two blocks that each declare `enum { BLA = 2 };` when a
  declaration is between them. The patch does not change this, because enumeration constants keep
  the exemption.
